$comment: Concord-authored additions to FedRAMP 2026 KSIs. Keyed by 2026 indicator ID.
FedRAMP authors the statement, name and control mappings
(fedramp-consolidated-rules.json); Concord authors only what is here.
rules: still empty. No phase-one rule is carried onto a 2026 indicator, and
a verdict rule is added only after reading that indicator's own statement.
methods: Concord platform posture checks curated per KSI (ccf.fedramp20x.methods).
The bar: the check's FAILURE must contradict the indicator's statement.
Sharing a mapped 800-53 control is not enough. A failing method raises the
KSI to warn; a passing one is evidence; neither makes it pass, because most
2026 KSIs describe a practice persistently reviewed, which configuration
cannot prove. Each rationale quotes the words the failure contradicts.

methods.rationale: Fails when neither FIDO2 nor certificate-based authentication is enabled, so no phishing-resistant method exists to satisfy "strong passwords with phishing-resistant MFA".
Fails when SMS, voice or email authentication is enabled; an interceptable factor contradicts "phishing-resistant MFA".
Fails when legacy authentication is not blocked; legacy protocols authenticate with a password alone, contradicting "strong passwords with phishing-resistant MFA".
Fails when a user has no MFA method registered; that user authenticates without MFA, contradicting "with phishing-resistant MFA".
Fails when the AWS root user has no MFA device; the most privileged account authenticating by password alone contradicts the statement.
Fails when the IAM password policy is below 14 characters or permits reuse of the last 24; contradicts "strong passwords".
Fails when ordinary accounts can create tenants, register applications or create security groups; that is access beyond "only ... the resources they need".
Fails when any member can invite external guests; granting outside access is not limited to those who need it.
Fails when an enabled account has been inactive over 90 days; an unused account keeps access it does not need, contradicting "can only access the resources they need".
Fails when a bucket does not block public access; anonymous access contradicts "each user or device can only access the resources they need".
Fails when an enabled account has been inactive over 90 days; an account whose lifecycle is managed would have been disabled, contradicting "the lifecycle ... of all accounts ... securely managed".

Fails when an active IAM access key is older than 90 days; long-lived static credentials for programmatic access contradict "appropriately secure authentication methods ... for non-user accounts and services".
Fails when a user flagged as risky has no disposition; an account left unsecured after suspicious activity contradicts "disabled or otherwise secured in response to suspicious activity".
Fails when no directory audit record exists in the last 7 days; directory modifications are not being logged, contradicting "Modifications ... are logged".
Fails when no multi-region CloudTrail trail is logging; AWS API changes are not logged, contradicting "Modifications ... are logged".
Fails when no multi-region trail is logging; AWS activity is not centrally logged, contradicting "centralized ... logging of events, activities, and changes".
Fails when a trail does not validate its log files; tampering would go undetected, contradicting "tamper-resistant logging".
Fails when no sign-in audit record exists in the last 7 days; sign-in events are not being logged, contradicting "to ensure these activities occur".
Fails when no directory audit record exists in the last 7 days; directory change events are not being logged.
Fails when no multi-region trail is logging; AWS API events are not being logged.
Fails when a VPC has no active flow log; network events for that VPC are not being logged.
Fails when a high or critical alert has gone unactioned for over 30 days; the security log is not being reviewed, contradicting "Logs are persistently reviewed".
Fails when a bucket has no default server-side encryption; objects stored unencrypted contradict "Information is encrypted or otherwise secured".
Fails when EBS encryption by default is off; new volumes are stored unencrypted.
Fails when a storage account does not encrypt blob and file data at rest.
Fails when no device compliance policy requires storage encryption; managed devices may hold information unencrypted.
Fails when a storage account accepts plain HTTP or TLS below 1.2; information in transit is not secured from "unwanted access or modification".
Fails when a bucket does not block public access; information is not secured from "unwanted access".
Fails when a database instance is reachable from the internet; information is not secured from "unwanted access".

Fails when a storage account accepts plain HTTP or TLS below 1.2; communications to it are not authenticated and integrity-protected, contradicting "authenticity and integrity of communications ... validated".
Fails when a trail does not validate its log files; the integrity of the audit log is not cryptographically validated, contradicting "Use cryptographic methods to validate the integrity".
Fails when an active access key is older than 90 days; secrets are not being regularly rotated, contradicting "regular rotation of ... secrets is automated".
Fails when a node's latest Puppet run failed; that node's configuration is not being managed, contradicting "managed using automation".
Fails when a node has not reported in 24 hours; its configuration is unmanaged and unreviewed for drift.
Fails when no Azure Policy assignment is enforcing; configuration is audited at most, not managed by automation.
Fails when no Organization Policy constraint applies to the project; configuration is not being managed by automation.
Fails when a managed device is out of compliance with its policy; configuration has drifted from its managed baseline, contradicting "persistently reviewed for drift".
Fails when a security group allows SSH or RDP from the internet; inbound traffic is not limited, contradicting "configured to limit inbound ... network traffic".
Fails when a database instance is reachable from the internet; inbound traffic to it is not limited.
Fails when SSH or RDP is exposed to the internet; an exposed administrative port contradicts "a minimal attack surface".
Fails when a database instance is reachable from the internet.
Fails when a bucket does not block public access.
Fails when Inspector does not scan EC2, ECR and Lambda; software on those resources is not automatically monitored for upstream vulnerabilities.
Fails when no Defender for Cloud plan is on the Standard tier; workloads are not automatically monitored for vulnerabilities.
Fails when a managed node has not reported in 24 hours; the inventory generated from PuppetDB is stale, contradicting "real-time inventories of all information resources".
